article_markdown:
# Claude Shannon — Information becomes a quantity

Shannon linked Boolean algebra to switching circuits and founded information theory. Entropy, channel capacity and coding theorems made communication limits mathematically precise.

Entropy measures average information under a distribution. For an independent identically distributed source, it controls asymptotic lossless compression rates.

H(X) = −Σₓ p(x) log₂ p(x)

## The right unit of information

An outcome of probability p has surprisal −log₂p. Averaging this over the source distribution gives entropy. A highly biased bit has entropy below one because its outcome is usually predictable.

H(X) = −Σₓ p(x) log₂ p(x)

```tex
H(X)=-\sum_x p(x)\log_2 p(x)
```

## Two limits, not one

Source coding concerns how far information can be compressed. Channel coding concerns how fast it can be transmitted reliably through noise. For a discrete memoryless channel, rates strictly below capacity allow codes with error tending to zero as block length grows.

R < C ⇒ error → 0

## Where graph theory enters

Zero-error communication is a different requirement from vanishing error. Confusability can be represented by a graph, leading to Shannon capacity and Lovász’s solution for the five-cycle.

Θ(C₅) = √5

## Try a code before taking a limit

Send one bit using 000 or 111. Majority decoding repairs one flipped position, at the cost of a rate of 1/3 information bit per transmitted bit. This finite example belongs to error correction. It makes the role of redundancy tangible before a channel-capacity theorem asks which rates are possible with increasingly long blocks.

Hamming’s profile takes this geometric view further. Blackwell’s profile asks another question: whether the received observation supports every decision available from a better one. Neither comparison turns entropy into a measure of meaning.

## Three directions to explore

1. How does typical-set compression work?

2. Why are zero-error and vanishing-error capacity different?

3. How can a graph encode confusable symbols?
